input: When a user click the button, the request are send to the server without no delay.
tests: Hard rule that errors do not affect the score, at the extreme: an error-riddled sentence whose corrected phrasing is fully native-like must score 5/5, with every error in §2 and zero Observations. Tests the most counterintuitive consequence of 'score the phrasing only' and that errors are never duplicated into Observations.
must_do: Flag 'user click' -> 'user clicks' as an Error (subject-verb agreement)
Flag 'request are send' -> 'request is sent' as an Error (agreement + valency)
Flag the double negative 'without no delay' -> 'without delay' / 'with no delay' as an Error (negation grammar)
Report no surviving Medium/High Observations (once errors are corrected, the phrasing is native-like)
Assign Naturalness Score 5/5 — errors do not affect the score (§1); with 0 surviving Medium/High the floor rule forces 5
Produce a Revised Sentence that fixes all errors and reads native-like
must_not_do: Lower the score below 5 because of the grammar errors ('Errors do not affect the score')
Reclassify any grammar error as an Observation, or duplicate the same fix into both Errors and Observations (forbidden by §2: an issue is either an Error or an Observation, never both)
Invent a phrasing Observation to justify a score below 5
Leave any of the three errors unflagged in the visible output
